open_points.subject: OwnerSession idle lifetime
open_points.text: “An owner request … restarts the 30 minutes” and “the instant of its last request” do not say whether that instant is the request’s arrival, admission or completion.
open_points.question: From which instant does the renewed 30-minute idle period run when an owner request takes time to complete?
options: The request’s arrival instant
The instant it passes session validation
The request’s completion instant
open_points.default_guess: Use the instant the request passes session validation.

open_points.subject: Confirmation input binding
open_points.text: The confirmation is bound to its inputs “kept as a digest of those values in a fixed order,” but the fixed order, encoding and normalization of those values are not declared.
open_points.question: What exact byte representation is digested so that confirmation-time inputs can be compared with the inputs originally shown?
options: Digest a canonical encoding of domain values after A02 normalization
Digest the raw submitted form fields in a declared field order
Digest a canonical State 6 request object
open_points.default_guess: Digest a canonical encoding of the normalized domain values in schema order.

open_points.subject: Create request id validation
open_points.text: A request id is “printable text of at most 128 characters,” but “printable” and the length measure are not defined.
open_points.question: Exactly which characters are accepted, and is the 128 limit measured in Unicode code points, encoded bytes or another unit?
options: Printable ASCII, limited by characters
Unicode graphic characters, limited by code points
Valid UTF-8 text, limited by encoded bytes
open_points.default_guess: Accept printable ASCII and count characters.

open_points.subject: Validation of records belonging to unpicked projects
open_points.text: Rule 1 says the mapping shows “every malformed record,” while rule 3 says records only of projects not picked “are neither checked” nor shown as conflicts.
open_points.question: Are malformed rooms and pointers belonging only to unpicked projects checked and reported, or completely ignored?
options: Ignore them unless their project is picked
Check and report them but do not let them refuse the import
Treat any malformed record anywhere in the file as refusing the upload or import
open_points.default_guess: Ignore them unless their project is picked, except for the explicitly global file and project-record checks.

open_points.subject: Duplicate ids involving unpicked projects
open_points.text: Rule 3 says records of unpicked projects “take no part in the duplicate-id check,” while rule 4 calls an id malformed when it “occurs twice among the file's records of one kind.”
open_points.question: Does a room or pointer id duplicated between a picked project and an unpicked project refuse the import?
options: No; only records brought in participate
Yes; duplicates are checked across the whole file
Only duplicate project ids are global; room and pointer ids are selection-scoped
open_points.default_guess: Only records brought in participate, while duplicate project records remain a global upload error under rule 3.

open_points.subject: Minimum secret length
open_points.text: “A secret … is at least 32 bytes long,” but the configuration representation and any decoding applied before measuring are not stated.
open_points.question: What value is measured for the 32-byte startup check?
options: The UTF-8 encoding of the configured text
Decoded bytes from a required textual encoding such as base64
Characters in the configured value
open_points.default_guess: Measure the UTF-8 bytes of the configured secret text.

open_points.subject: Backup run outcome
open_points.text: Each run writes “its outcome,” but one run can independently succeed or fail at temporary-file cleanup, backup creation/checking and deletion of expired backups.
open_points.question: What outcome is recorded and shown when, for example, a checked backup is kept but deletion of an expired backup fails?
options: One overall failure outcome
A successful-backup outcome with a separate deletion failure
A structured outcome recording each phase
open_points.default_guess: Record a structured outcome for cleanup, backup/check and retention deletion separately.

open_points.subject: Order and continuation of backup-run phases
open_points.text: Rule 4 makes temporary-file cleanup first, rule 5 requires expired-backup deletion whether the new backup succeeds or not, and rule 6 does not say whether a deletion failure prevents creation of the new backup.
open_points.question: After preliminary cleanup or retention deletion fails, which remaining phases of that run still execute, and in what order?
options: Cleanup, retention deletion, then backup; continue after retention failure
Cleanup, backup/check, then retention deletion; continue after backup failure
Stop all remaining phases after any failure
open_points.default_guess: Run cleanup first, then backup/check, then retention deletion; still attempt retention deletion after backup failure.

open_points.subject: Failed backup cleanup
open_points.text: Rule 4 anticipates files left under the temporary prefix and says a failed removal leaves them for a later start or run, while rule 6 says “A backup or a deletion that fails leaves no partial file.”
open_points.question: May a failed backup or failed cleanup leave a temporary partial file in the backup location?
options: Yes, under the declared temporary prefix for later cleanup
No; failure must remove every partial file before the run ends
Only a cleanup-removal failure may leave one
open_points.default_guess: Only a cleanup-removal failure may leave a temporary prefixed file; ordinary backup failures must clean theirs up.

open_points.subject: Retention-review record for ended relationships after restore
open_points.text: R0-89 says the governance names each repeated action “by its date, kind and the customer_ref or project_id it touched,” but ending a relationship can use an effective date earlier than the action date.
open_points.question: For an end-of-relationship action, does the recorded date mean the action date or the effective relationship-end date needed to reproduce the Customer state?
options: The effective relationship-end date
The date the action was performed
Both dates
open_points.default_guess: Record both, and replay the effective relationship-end date.

open_points.subject: Audit-erasure cutoff restored from governance
open_points.text: R0-89 and A18 refer to “the latest date audit entries were erased by,” while A15 permits accepted erasures with cutoff dates in any non-future order.
open_points.question: Is the cutoff replayed after restore the cutoff from the most recently performed erasure, or the greatest cutoff date ever applied?
options: The greatest cutoff date ever applied
The cutoff used by the most recently performed erasure
Every recorded cutoff replayed in action order
open_points.default_guess: Use the greatest cutoff date ever applied.
